predicates.name: EcomStockLocationCategory
predicates._why: Replace, whole table: the two stock location categories the base's own rows point at (EcomStockLocation.StockLocationCategoryId STOCKLOCCAT1 and STOCKLOCCAT2, and the Customer pickup delivery method SHIP5 whose stock-location provider lists the STOCKLOCCAT1 locations). The stock DW10 setup wizard creates the table empty, so a blank DW10 database had pickup locations in a category that does not exist; the base now ships 'Click and collect' and 'Warehouse' on the same ids and identities (4, 5) the Swift-derived databases carried (Foundry #1352).

predicates.name: EcomStockLocation
predicates._why: Replace, whole table: the stock locations are framework configuration, not catalogue. The baseline DB shipped the Swift demo's own rows (1 'BikeShop Copenhagen', 2 'BikeShop Aarhus', 3 'Default stock location'), so every composed edition carried a bike shop's warehouse names. The base now owns the table outright with neutral names on the SAME ids 1-3: the sample-data layer's EcomStockUnit rows and EcomShops.ShopStockLocationID reference those ids, so a rekey would orphan them (Foundry #1303). Replace rather than Merge so a re-deserialize restores the neutral set instead of leaving a previously delivered bike-shop name in place. StockLocationCategoryId stays 1 and 3 -> STOCKLOCCAT1 'Click and collect', 2 -> STOCKLOCCAT2 'Warehouse'; both categories ship in the base's own EcomStockLocationCategory predicate, and the base's own Customer pickup delivery method needs pickup locations sitting in that category.

predicates.name: EcomStockLocationTranslations
predicates._why: Replace, whole table: the display name a Dynamicweb stock location actually renders lives here, not in EcomStockLocation.StockLocationName. The baseline ships 1|ENU 'BikeShop Copenhagen', 2|ENU 'BikeShop Aarhus' (description 'Warehouse west') and 3|ENU 'Default stock location', so correcting only the parent table would have left the bike shop's names on every delivered host (Foundry #1303). Same ids and the same ENU key as the parent predicate, names matched to it, descriptions empty. The table has no identity column, so the composite PK (StockLocationId + LanguageId) is the whole key.

predicates.name: EcomProductGroupField
predicates._why: Replace, whole table: the seven Swift 2 product group fields the Swift 2.4 navigation, group list and group poster templates read (ProductGroupPromotionImage, ProductGroupPromotionDescription, ProductGroupPromotionLink, ProductGroupPromotionLinkLabel, ProductGroupNavigationImage, ProductGroupRelatedContent, SelectedGroup), on Swift's own ids GROUPFIELD1..GROUPFIELD10 so a database that already carries Swift's definitions is updated in place and never gets a second definition of the same system name. DW10 stores each group field as a physical EcomGroups column that the stock setup wizard does not create; schemaSync EcomGroupFields makes the Serializer add every missing column right after these rows are written (Serializer CustomColumnSchemaSync, type from EcomFieldType), so the sample-data EcomGroups rows that carry the seven columns land on a blank DW10 database (Foundry #1352).

predicates.name: Reference category
predicates._why: Replace, filtered to the ONE hidden template category Dynamicweb's completeness-rule and category-field admin UI reads (CategoryType 2). BASE.md has claimed this row since 3.0.0 and it never shipped - the Foundry gate synthesised it as Step 3b instead (tools/harness/Invoke-SeedVerify.ps1, DemoVerifier Check 2), which means a consumer deserializing the Distribution without the gate never got it (Foundry #1304). Filtered, never whole-table: the tc_* concrete categories are sample-data-owned merge rows and a whole-table Replace here would wipe them.

predicates.name: Reference category translation
predicates._why: Replace, filtered to the reference_category rows only, for the same reason as the parent predicate: the ENU display name 'Reference category' ships with the row it belongs to, while the tc_* translations stay sample-data-owned merge rows. The Foundry gate's own seed is IF NOT EXISTS-guarded on the category id, so a gated host that already carries a LANG1 row is unaffected (Foundry #1304).

predicates.name: EcomOrderStates
predicates._why: Replace, whole table, NO nameColumn: the files are named by the key OrderStateId. Order state names repeat across flows (New is OS1, OS8 and OS11; Draft is OS5 and OS10; Rejected is OS3 and OS7), and Serializer 1.0.6-beta takes a nameColumn value as the row identity, so the same-name documents were merged later-wins and OS7, OS8, OS10 and OS11 never reached a blank DW10 database (measured on foundry-blank-dw10.mydwsite4.com, gate run 20260928-183202; justdynamics/Truvio.Commerce.Serializer#38). Keyed by id, every state is its own row.

predicates.name: Customer center user groups
predicates.where: AccessUserType = 2 AND AccessUserName IN ('Customers','Account Admin','CSR','Employees','Find dealers')

predicates.name: EcomNumbers
predicates._why: Merge, filtered to the eight counters that mint the ids the base ships (PAY3, SHIP13, OS14, GROUPFIELD10, CREL3002, VATGRP2, SHOP1, LANG1), keyed by the wizard's NumberId. raiseOnlyColumns NumberCounter (Serializer 1.0.7-beta, Foundry #1322): a counter is written as the larger of the host value and the shipped value, so a blank database mints the next unused id and a live host whose counter is ahead keeps it. The other columns follow Merge and never overwrite the host's row (Distribution #103).
